subject: POC / Trial planning: success criteria, model selection, multilingual support
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC / Trial planning: success criteria, model selection, multilingual support

Hi Daniel — great to meet earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side for the POC/trial so we can get to a scoped evaluation quickly.

Recap from discovery:
- Primary use: customer support triage + short-answer automation for Acme Retail support portal.
- Expected load for POC: ~1k requests/day, bursts to 5k/day.
- Multilingual surface: EN + ES (priority), FR second priority; some PT and DE later.
- Success measures: accuracy (resolution rate on top-1), average latency (p50 < 300ms), and cost per 1k tokens under target.

Proposed POC plan (high level):
1) 2-week sandbox setup (data push + sample traffic) — Redwood will provide a dedicated trial instance.
2) 3-week evaluation window with live-ish traffic or replay.
3) Success criteria and evaluation template attached (ACME_Redwood_POC_Success_Criteria.pdf and evaluation_template.xlsx).

Model recommendation for the trial (initial):
- Primary: Mistral-7B-Instruct (good instruction-following and cost profile).
- Fallback: Llama-2-13b-chat (lower latency on our Dedicated instances and handles some multilingual cases).
- If Spanish/FR performance is insufficient, we can test fine-tuned or instruction-tuned variants or a larger multilingual base for a focused subset.

Ownership & next steps:
- Redwood (Marissa): stand up trial instance, provide test credentials, and load sample prompt set.
- ACME (Daniel / Priya): share representative sample logs and priority intents; confirm 2-week sandbox start date.
- Redwood (Ben): provide evaluation dashboard + instrumentation.

Can you confirm the sample data ETA and whether EN+ES is sufficient for the first pass? If yes, I’ll schedule the sandbox provisioning for next week.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: ACME_Redwood_POC_Success_Criteria.pdf (application/pdf), evaluation_template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: success criteria, model selection, multilingual support

Thanks Marissa — that looks great. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Sample data ETA: we can export a 7-day sample of anonymized support transcripts by Friday (2026-07-17).
- For the first pass, EN+ES is sufficient. We have ~12% ES volume and would prioritize EN + ES coverage.
- Success criteria: can you add a raw NRR (no response required) metric for triage accuracy and a false-positive rate for automated replies?

About models: we prefer smaller models for latency/cost reasons but need to ensure Spanish handling is solid. Mistral-7B-Instruct sounds good as the primary; for fallback we are open to Llama-2-13b-chat. If we need to test a multilingual base, what would you recommend for Spanish-first performance?

Also can you confirm whether Redwood will handle tokenization/encoding disparities for Spanish (accents/orthography) or if we need to normalize?

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Park | Head of Product, Acme Retail
daniel.park@acme.com | +1 617-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC / Trial planning: success criteria, model selection, multilingual support

Thanks Daniel — good questions. Short answers below and then a proposed concrete plan.

- Metrics: we’ll add NRR and false-positive rate to the evaluation template — included in the attached spreadsheet.
- Spanish normalization: Redwood’s inference pipeline includes standard Unicode normalization and we can add lightweight token-cleaning for accents if you prefer; for most modern instruction models we recommend leaving original orthography intact. We’ll flag tokenization diffs in the evaluation dashboard.
- Multilingual recommendation: if ES performance on Mistral-7B-Instruct is below threshold during the first week, we propose testing a larger multilingual model (e.g., Llama-2-70B-chat or a dedicated multilingual variant) but for cost control we’d only spin that up for targeted intents.

Concrete next steps and timeline:
1) Fri 2026-07-17: ACME shares anonymized 7-day logs. (Daniel / Priya)
2) Mon 2026-07-20: Redwood provisions sandbox instance and loads prompt set. (Marissa)
3) Tue 2026-07-21 to Mon 2026-08-10: 3-week evaluation window with our instrumentation running. (Ben owns dashboards)
4) By Wed 2026-08-12: joint review with success metrics and recommendation for GA configuration.

Model fallback logic we’ll configure for the trial:
- Default route: Mistral-7B-Instruct on Redwood Dedicated.
- If latency > 500ms or model confidence below a per-intent threshold -> route to Llama-2-13b-chat (quantized) as fallback.
- For ES-heavy intents we’ll monitor token-level differences and can route those intents to the larger multilingual model if needed.

I’ll start the provisioning once we get the logs Friday. Ben, can you prepare the dashboard with NRR/false-positive and p50/p95 latency buckets? Aditya, please add notes on model quantization profile for the fallback (L2-13b quantized to 4-bit derivation).

Thanks — will follow up once sandbox is up.

—Marissa
